title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon reduction with H-prime semiprime walks, sort-based matching, drawn coins, capacity and caps

claims.statement: Setting: BLS12-381 G1, generator P0 of prime order r, d=2^20 (6d divides r-1), input T=A_1=[s]P0 and A_i=[s^i]P0, i<=n, n>=2^20 (only T and A_d are read, so the bound holds for every n>=2^20 including 2^20), s uniform in 1..r-1. Claim: the classical attack of proof.md recovers s with success probability at least 0.39 for every input and over fresh algorithm coins, using at most 2^116.8172 total target-group-operation equivalents (one equivalent = one batched incomplete affine G1 addition = 2000 AArch64 instructions, C=2000), including all preprocessing (at most 2^115.83, included), randomness, capped prime searches, failed runs, record routing, sorting, matching, caps, verification, output and the final scalar check; peak memory at most 2^124.1 bytes (2^84 owner, 2^20 generating and 2^31 storage nodes, each counted at its full 2^40 bytes); no advice, no quantum step, no retry. Attack (proof.md Sections 2-8): Cheon's reduction to z=s^d in the order-m subgroup H of d-th powers, m=(r-1)/2^20. The attack draws t uniform in F_r^* and tau uniform in F_r^*: it works on T'=[t]T and A'_d=[t^d]A_d, so z'=t^d z is uniform on H for every input and the success probability is exactly |S|/m with S the set of z values of the pair list; every base point is scaled by tau, so every record key is a function of the drawn coins and the key ensemble is not a fixed key set. Baby and giant scalars are products a*w of two H-primes (primes q with q^m=1 mod r), w from the list W of the first 2^50 H-primes above 2^39 and a from disjoint lists of H-primes in (2^77,2^96), each list built by one capped segmented sieve (candidate caps 2^78 and 2^94 odd integers, about 5x the expected scan) that trial-divides every candidate by every prime below the square root of the interval top, 2^40 for W and 2^48 for the base lists, so every survivor is prime by complete trial division and there is no Miller-Rabin base set and no primality probability; one 234-bit square-and-multiply mod r per surviving prime, charged at the number of primes the capped interval holds (2^73.26 and 2^88.99, Dusart's bound); the search itemises at 2^78.17 and 2^93.90 units and is charged 2^79 and 2^95; a cap reached with too few H-primes fails the run and is charged 2^-40. Each chain advances by one batched incomplete affine addition per step from a table of even multiples [g]Q, g<=2^33. The N=2^115.6644 baby and N giant points (6N^2/m=0.52) give 224-bit keys (bits 1..224 of the even one of y, p-y) invariant under the six GLV/negation automorphisms. The 2N=2^116.6644 records of 48 bytes are matched on a shared-nothing cluster with 2^40 bytes of RAM per node and no remote-memory instruction: the per-node record capacity C=(2^40 - 2^38.5546 bytes of auxiliaries)/96=2^32.7549 records fixes the node count at every stage, since a pass must hold 2N records somewhere, so 2N needs at least 2N/C=2^83.9095 receiving nodes and the cluster uses S=2^84 forwarding and owner nodes (three 28-bit address digits), giving mu=2N/S=2^32.6644 records per node per stage; each record is routed by 3 passes on 28-bit digits of the 84-bit key prefix (29 instructions each: 19 control including the block-base add, the madd that adds 48*fill_count and the fill-count writeback, 4 for the full-block posting share, 6 transport copy) and sorted by 2 local LSD passes on 28-bit digits (25 each) to a 140-bit sort prefix, then scanned once (10); after the third pass each owner drains its arriving records into its sort buffer (10). Success: the birthday model on S gives 1-e^-0.52=0.4054795, less a flat 0.01 model allowance (10x the 0.11 percentage point deviation measured at toy scale), less per-node cap bounds (2^-35.01, 2^-6192, 2^-67.98 at the 2^20-comparison and 128-verification caps), less node and pass overflow (Chernoff on [0,12]-bounded orbit loads, load factor C/mu=1.0648 for the bucket and 1.0608 for a digit slab, 2^-1.68e6 and 2^-2^76.5) and 2^-40 for the search caps: success >= 0.3954794 >= 0.39. The posting charge is one global total over the whole run: 3*[(2N/25)*100 + (2^84+2^20+2^31)*2^28*107] + 107*2^20*2^84 = 2^121.2894 instructions, carried exactly by the 4-per-record-per-pass share, the final-block row and the pass-1 marker row, with no per-node bound on the records a node handles (a generating node streams 2^96.6644 records and holds none) and no mean; each pass is an exchange along one address digit and every stage's inbound is at most C per node (every pass at most its own digit slab's count over 2^56, i.e. N_a/2^56 + 26*2^20 <= C with a digit-slab Chernoff bound (N_a a sum of [0,12]-bounded orbit contributions of mean mu*2^56 = 2^88.6644, threshold factor 1.0608, 2^-2^76.5 per slab, union over the 3*2^28 (pass, digit) pairs), the owner bucket mu with 2^-1.68e6), the records of a pass being held in one of the node's two C-record buffers while it routes the other out; the two buffers, the open-block area and the receive ring with per-block credits give a deadlock-free schedule (no receiver's copy-out waits on a sender) and the final block per destination detects the end of each pass, pass 1's markers being one per (generating node, owner) pair; W and the base lists are arrays of 16-byte fields (value in bits 0..96; every accepted base prime is below 2^96; 16-bit tag in bits 112..127) on the 2^31 storage nodes, a label resolved by a request/reply whose cost is inside the verification cap, and the walk stream reads one field per record; all F_r arithmetic is priced at a 128-instruction 4-limb Montgomery multiply. Ledger (unit 2000 instructions): 2Nc=2^116.8084 plus 2^109.4554 of fixed rows = 2^116.817200, score 292043/2500.

experiments.purpose: mode all (the single initial run) runs ledger, coverage, distinct and ec, about 8 s. ledger: exact recomputation of the per-record row (210 itemised), the 84-bit owner id with its three 28-bit routing digits, the node count derived from the record capacity C (2N/C and the per-stage load table), the record and 16-byte prime-field layouts, the global posting total 3*[(2N/25)*100 + (2^84+2^20+2^31)*2^28*107] + 107*2^20*2^84 and its equality with the three rows that carry it, the layout alternatives, the two 28-bit LSD passes and the 140-bit sort prefix, every per-node fixed row, the capped H-prime searches with their itemised sieve, per-segment table and H-test costs and their charged values and the 128-instruction F_r multiply, the per-node run-pair and verification caps with their failure bounds, node capacity and its Chernoff margins for a bucket and for a pass, the success line, memory, the storage-node field budget, and the exact integer score (smallest k with W^10000 <= 2^k). coverage: scalar-level toy success at three primes against the diagonal-corrected Poisson model. distinct: occupied residues over all baby/giant ratios at one toy, the support for the success-set model allowance. ec: Algorithm A end to end on toy j=0 curves with truncated keys, a false-match cap, and the d-th root selected by matching T before the recovered scalar is compared. Each mode can be rerun with more trials. Toy results are evidence at toy scale only.
